title: VPC Network Guardrail Module: Subnet Patterns, NAT/IGW Failover, Endpoints & Upgrade Hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that standardizes VPC connectivity guardrails for Private deployments. The module will provide prescriptive subnet patterns (public / private / isolated), automated NAT/IGW provisioning with multi-path failover, managed VPC endpoints (gateway + interface), typed routing table generation, and built-in upgrade hooks and health checks. It should be consumable by customers running Redwood Private in VPCs and by internal automation for on-prem blueprints. Key goals: (1) predictable egress behavior and cost visibility, (2) safe Terraform upgrades with minimal disruption, (3) automated health probes for endpoint/egress path viability, (4) clear observability outputs for Console and SRE playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables to create named subnet tiers: public, app-private, infra-private, isolated-backend
Supports single and multi-AZ deployments with consistent route table mapping per AZ
Creates NAT Gateways (or NAT instances via opt-in) with automatic failover routing and optional IGW-only egress pattern
Provision VPC endpoints: gateway endpoints for S3/Dynamo + configurable interface endpoints with private DNS toggles
Routing resource abstraction supports weighted egress paths and explicit route priorities (customer-configurable)
Health check stack deploys a lightweight probe (lambda / cloudwatch synthetic) per AZ that validates: endpoint reachability, NAT egress success, and route table drift detection
Module can be upgraded in-place: uses resource replacement minimization, stable IDs for TF state, and an opt-in migration plan for route changes
Terraform plan shows no destructive changes for default minor-version upgrades; major changes require opt-in via var 'apply_migration = true'
Module includes a test harness: unit tests with terratest, integration smoke tests in a CI sandbox, and a step-by-step migration playbook in docs
technical_notes:
- Implement with Terraform 1.5+ and AWS provider >= 5.0. Avoid provider alias proliferation; expose provider as an optional provider input.
- Subnet naming: <env>-<tier>-<az>-<index> to support predictable routing table tags.
- Use lifecycle 'prevent_destroy' only for critical resources (e.g. IGW) and provide clear migration docs when toggled.
- NAT strategy: default managed NAT Gateways per AZ behind an autoscaling EIP pool; optional flag `use_nat_instances` for constrained environments.
- Failover: maintain route table entries named with priority metadata; use AWS route replacement on health-failure events triggered by the probe.
- VPC endpoints: create gateway endpoints for S3/Dynamo by default; interface endpoints are opt-in with security_group_ids input. Use aws_vpc_endpoint_service_allowed_principals when integrating with PrivateLink services.
- Health checks: ship an optional stack (CloudFormation via 'local_file' + 'aws_cloudformation_stack' or Terraform native constructs) that deploys a small Lambda runner which performs periodic checks and writes metrics to CloudWatch. Implement a 'route_repair' SNS -> Lambda flow as opt-in.
- Upgrades: maintain tfstate resource address immutability where possible, provide migration helper scripts (terraform state mv) and a `preflight_check` module that runs in CI to detect risky diffs.
- Observability: outputs include NAT usage reports (bytes/flows), endpoint status booleans, and route drift flag. Those map to Console dashboards via a predefined metrics namespace.
tasks: Design module public interface (variables, outputs) and publish RFC (doc link in links)
Implement subnet pattern generation with per-AZ map and optional custom CIDR blocks
Implement NAT + IGW provisioning with failover route logic
Implement VPC endpoints (gateway + interface) with security group integration
Build health check stack (lambda + cw metrics + optional auto-repair SNS)
Write terratest unit tests and CI pipeline job definitions
Author upgrade/migration playbook and sample migration plan scripts
Add telemetry outputs and Console dashboard wiring (metrics namespace + recommended alerts)
Code review, security review, and bake in staging sandbox

notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: 1) state-stability for route table refactors, 2) security posture around interface endpoints and private DNS, 3) failure modes for NAT EIP exhaustion and suggested guardrails. See technical_notes for suggested mitigations.
migration_playbook_summary: 1) Run preflight_check to detect route conflicts and resource drift. 2) If terraform plan includes route replacements, set var apply_migration=true in a staged rollout to one AZ. 3) Monitor 'redwood/vpc-guardrail' metrics; if route_repair triggers, investigate logs in CloudWatch and rollback by toggling apply_migration=false. 4) For destructive changes flagged, run provided terraform state mv helper scripts before apply.
test_plan: Unit: terratest for subnet naming and route table generation. Integration: create ephemeral sandbox VPC in CI, apply module with default config, run health-check probes for 10 minutes, assert endpoint booleans and NAT metrics are emitted. Canary upgrade: deploy v1 -> v1.1 change that adds optional interface endpoints, run migration_playbook and assert zero service interruption in sandbox. Logs stored in s3://redwood-ci-artifacts/ENG-77771/
implementation_notes:
- Keep module atomic and small; split health checks into a 'guardrail-observability' child module so customers can opt-out.
- Avoid hard-coded account IDs; accept a map of endpoint_service_configs for cross-account PrivateLink.
- Use semantic versioning; bump major when default behaviors change (e.g., swapping NAT to centralized egress).
